answer: The binder sews every book on the frame and counts the stitches, entering the binding in his tally against the owner. A quartz book bound elsewhere fails the tally: at the ledge of the frame the thread must match the binder's own sewing, and a strange binding falls apart within a year. Forging a binding means hiring a binder, buying false leather and paying 8,600, and the harbor entry in the frame tally is kept by the library, so a book whose stitches were never counted is unbound.
